en: The large, usually yellowish-green or black, savory fruit of the avocado tree.
The avocado tree, Persea americana, of the laurel family.
Of a dull yellowish-green colour.

avocado.ety:
Borrowed from Latin American Spanish avocado, from the earlier aguacate, which comes from Classical Nahuatl āhuacatl (“avocado”). Doublet of abacate. Compare aguacatillo, avocadillo.
The first mention can be found in a catalogue of Jamaican plants in 1696.

ex.en: The avocado is rich in fats.
ex.ja: アボカドには脂肪分が豊富に含まれています。

ex.en: Avocados are rich in vitamin E.
ex.ja: アボカドはビタミンＥが豊富です。

ex.en: The avocado is rich in nutrients.
ex.ja: アボカドは栄養豊富です。

note.ja: スペイン語 aguacate の変化形。ナワトル語（アステカの言語）āhuacatl に由来する。

en: An instance of bashing; a physical or verbal attack.
A large container for holding water in which a person may bathe (take a bath).

ex.en: Tom filled the bathtub up with hot water.
ex.ja: トムはお風呂を入れた。

ex.en: He has the water running in the bathtub.
ex.ja: 彼は浴槽に水を出しっぱなしにしている。

ex.en: Tom filled the bathtub with hot water.
ex.ja: トムはお風呂を入れた。

note.ja: bath（風呂）+ tub（おけ）。「浴槽」。

en: The sound produced by the horn of a car, or any similar sound.
A short, electronically produced tone.
To produce a beep sound.
To have sexual intercourse with (someone), referring to the bleep tone used to censor obscene words in broadcasts.

ex.en: Leave your message after hearing the beep.
ex.ja: 発信音が聞こえた後であなたのメッセージを残してください。

ex.en: Did you hear your computer beep?
ex.ja: 自分のパソコンから警告音が鳴ってるの、聞こえた？

ex.en: I'm not at home now. Please leave a message after the beep.
ex.ja: ただいま留守にしております。ピーッという音が鳴りましたら、ご用件をお話しください。

note.ja: 擬音語。「ピー」。

en: One who benefits or receives an advantage.
One who benefits from the distribution, especially out of a trust or estate.
Holding some office or valuable possession, in subordination to another; holding under a feudal or other superior; having a dependent and…
Bestowed as a gratuity.

beneficiary.ety: From Latin beneficiarius (“enjoying a favor, granted a privilege”) from beneficium (“benefit”), perhaps via or influenced by French bénéficiaire (“beneficiary”). Indirectly, by way of the etymology of the Latin word beneficium, the English word beneficiary ultimately has the same origin as the English word benefactor, its near antonym.

en: The quality of having a bitter taste.
The quality of feeling bitter; acrimony, resentment; the quality of exhibiting such feelings.

bitterness.ety: From Middle English bitternesse, biternesse, from Old English biternes (“bitterness; grief”), equivalent to bitter + -ness.

ex.en: I can't look at this photograph without bitterness.
ex.ja: この写真を見る度に、心が痛みます。

note.ja: bitter（苦い）+ -ness。「苦さ・恨み」。bitter は bite（かむ）と同じ祖先。

en: Obvious, on show; unashamed; loudly obtrusive or offensive.

blatant.ety:
Coined by Edmund Spenser in 1596 in "blatant beast". Probably a variation of *blatand (Scots blaitand (“bleating”)), present participle of blate, a variation of bleat, equivalent to blate + -ant. See bleat. In addition, it is suggested by Latin blatiō (“speak like a fool, prate”), which is rare, and so the similitude may be just coincidental.
Compare typologically Bulgarian вопиющ (vopijušt), Russian вопию́щий (vopijúščij) (akin to вопи́ть (vopítʹ)).

ex.en: I glared at him with a blatant look of disapproval on my face.
ex.ja: 露骨に嫌な顔をして、彼を睨みつけた。

note.ja: 16世紀の詩人スペンサーの造語とされる。「騒々しい」→「あからさまな」。

en: A good thing; a thing to be thankful for or to appreciate duly.
That which is asked or granted as a benefit or favor; a gift or benefaction.
Gay; merry; jovial; convivial.

boon.ety: From Middle English boon (“prayer”), from Old Norse bón (“prayer, petition”), from Proto-Germanic *bōniz (“supplication”), influenced by boon (“good, favorable”, adjective). Doublet of ben; see there for more.

ex.en: This dictionary is great boon up to us.
ex.ja: この辞書は私たちにとってありがたいものだ。

en: A turbot or flatfish.
A rough cloak or ragged garment.
To act in a bratty manner as the submissive.
Characteristic of a confident and assertive woman.

brat.ety:
Early Modern English (c. 1500) slang term meaning "beggar's child". Possibly from Scots bratchet (“bitch, hound”), in which case it would be a doublet of brachet. Another possibility is that it was originally a dialectal word, from northern and western England and the Midlands, for a "makeshift or ragged garment," from Old English bratt (“cloak”), which is from a Celtic source (Old Irish brat (“cloak, cloth”)).
In the sense "characteristic of a confident and assertive woman", coined by English singer and songwriter Charli XCX in her 2024 album Brat, though occasional earlier uses of the word w

ex.en: For a brat, you've said something very mature.
ex.ja: がきにしては、随分大人びたことを言ったな。

ex.en: Tom is a brat.
ex.ja: トムはガキンチョよ。

ex.en: You shouldn't allow your son to act like a selfish brat.
ex.ja: 息子にわがままさせてはいけないよ。

ja: （船・列車の）寝台（bunk bed：二段ベッド）

en: One of a series of berths or beds placed in tiers.
A built-in bed on board ship, often erected in tiers one above the other.
To occupy a bunk.
To provide a bunk.

bunk.ety: Sense of sleeping berth possibly from Scottish Scottish English bunker (“seat, bench”), the origin of which is uncertain but possibly Scandinavian (North Germanic); compare Old Swedish bunke (“boards used to protect the cargo of a ship”). Possibly related to bunch.

ex.en: We often bunk off school.
ex.ja: 僕たち、よく学校をサボってます。

note.ja: bunker の短縮とされる。「（船の）寝台」。bunk bed（二段ベッド）。

en: Impartial and free from prejudice.
Straightforward, open and sincere, whether people find either refreshing or distasteful.
A spontaneous or unposed photograph.

candid.ety:
Etymology tree

ex.ja: 面接では、虚心坦懐に話すことが必要だ。

ex.en: I like him in that he is honest and candid.
ex.ja: 私は彼が正直で気さくであるから彼が好きだ。

ex.en: Listen to his candid opinion.
ex.ja: 彼の率直な意見に耳を傾けなさい。

note.ja: ラテン語 candidus（白い・純粋な）から。「率直な・ありのままの」。candidate（白衣の候補者）、candle と同じ。

en: Someone who takes care of a place or thing; someone looking after a place, or responsible for keeping it in good repair.
Synonym of caregiver (“a person who provides care to another”).
Temporary, on a short term basis.

ex.en: The accident was due to the negligence of the caretaker.
ex.ja: その事故の責任は管理人の怠慢にある。

note.ja: care（世話）+ taker（引き受ける人）。「管理人」→「暫定の」。

en: A list of tasks to be completed, names to be consulted, conditions to be verified and similar.
An inventory, especially of species.
To add to a checklist.

note.ja: check（確認）+ list（一覧）。「チェックリスト」。

en: A brace, band, or clasp for strengthening or holding things that are apart together.
An instrument used to temporarily shut off blood vessels, etc.
To fasten in place or together with (or as if with) a clamp.
To hold or grip tightly.

clamp.ety:
From Middle Dutch clamp, klampe (“a clamp, hook”), from Proto-Germanic *klampō (“clamp, clasp, cramp”), related to Proto-West Germanic *klammjan.
Cognate with Middle Low German klampe (“hook, clasp”), German Klampfe, Klampe (“clamp, cleat”), Norwegian klamp (“clamp”), Alemannic German Chlempi.

ex.en: The government clamped down on the minority group.
ex.ja: 政府は少数派を弾圧した。

ex.en: A wise businessman knows how to clamp down on costs.
ex.ja: 賢明な経営者はコストをぎりぎりまでさげる方法を知っていますよ。

note.ja: 中世オランダ語 klampe（留め金）から。「締めつける道具」→「取り締まる（clamp down）」。

ex.ja: 輸出市場での競争力強化が緊急の課題である。

en: A union or alliance of states or political organizations.
The act of forming an alliance.

confederation.ety: From Middle English confederacion, confideracion and Middle French confédération, from Old French confederacion, from Latin cōnfoederātiō. Doublet of confederacy.

note.ja: confederate（同盟する）+ -ion。con + foedus（盟約）。「連合」。federal と同じ。

Something told in confidence; a secret.

From confidential + -ity.

en: The act of contradicting.
A statement that contradicts itself, i.e., a statement that claims that the same thing is true and that it is false at the same time and …

contradiction.ety: From Middle English contradiccioun, contradiction, from Old French contradiction, from Latin contrādictiō, from contrādīcō (“speak against”).

ex.en: These facts admit of no contradiction.
ex.ja: これらの事実には反駁の余地がない。

ex.en: A contradiction has immediately appeared.
ex.ja: さっそく矛盾が出てきてる。

ex.ja: 彼の票決記録をたどると矛盾だらけです。

note.ja: contra（反対に）+ dict（言う）+ ion。反対のことを言うこと →「矛盾・反論」。

en: An act of investing with a crown; a crowning.
An act or the ceremony of formally investing a sovereign or the sovereign's consort with a crown and other insignia of royalty, on or sho…

Corōnō is derived from corōna (“garland, wreath; c

note.ja: ラテン語 coronare（冠をかぶせる）から。corona（冠）。「戴冠式」。crown と同じ語源。

en: A dry, thin, crispy baked bread (usually salty or savoury, but sometimes sweet, as in the case of graham crackers and animal crackers).
A prawn cracker.

cracker.ety:
From Middle English craker (“a boaster”), equivalent to crack (“to break, snap, utter, make a sound”) + -er. From crack (verb), the sound made when one is broken. The hard "bread" and "biscuit" sense is first attested in 1739.
The computing senses of cracker, crack, and cracking were promoted in the 1980s as an alternative to hacker, by programmers concerned about negative public associations of hack, hacking (“creative computer coding”). See Citations:cracker.
Various theories exist regarding the term's application to poor white Southerners. One theory holds that it originated with disadvanta

ex.en: He lived on crackers and water for three days.
ex.ja: 彼はビスケットと水で三日間命をつないだ。

ex.en: Mum, the rice crackers have gone soft and they don't taste good anymore.
ex.ja: お母さん、このおせんべい、しけってておいしくないよ。

ex.en: Mum, the rice crackers have gotten damp and they're not nice anymore.
ex.ja: お母さん、このおせんべい、しけってておいしくないよ。

note.ja: crack（パリッと割れる）+ -er。「パリッとしたもの」→「クラッカー・爆竹」。

en: Sly; crafty; clever in surreptitious behaviour.
Practical knowledge or experience; aptitude in performance; skill, proficiency; dexterity.
Practical skill employed in a secret or crafty manner; craft; artifice; skillful deceit; art or magic.

cunning.ety: From Middle English cunning, kunning, konnyng, alteration of earlier Middle English cunninde, kunnende, cunnand, from Old English cunnende, present participle of cunnan (“to know how to, be able to”), equivalent to con + -ing. Cognate with Scots cunnand (“cunning”), German könnend (“able to do”), Icelandic kunnandi (“cunning”). More at con, can.

ex.en: That's just how cunning North Korea is (and China, too).
ex.ja: それだけ北朝鮮は（中国も）狡猾なんです。

ex.en: People say that the fox is more cunning than other animals.
ex.ja: キツネは他の動物よりずる賢いと言われています。

ex.en: I see Tom as cunning rather than clever.
ex.ja: トムは賢いというよりずる賢いイメージだな。

note.ja: 古英語 cunnan（知っている）から。can と同じ祖先。「知恵がある」→「ずる賢い」。

en: A lifelike image of something, either verbal or visual.
A drawing or painting.

depiction.ety: From French dépiction, from Latin dēpictiō. By surface analysis, depict + -ion.

ex.en: Dickens' thoughts come across along with the vivid depiction of old London.
ex.ja: ディッケンズの考えが、ロンドンの下町の生き生きした描写と共に読者には伝わる。

note.ja: de（完全に）+ pict（描く）+ ion。描き出すこと →「描写」。depict（描写する）。

en: Used up, expended; of which nothing is left.
Of or pertaining to diabetes, especially diabetes mellitus.
Having diabetes, especially diabetes mellitus.
A person with diabetes, usually diabetes mellitus.
The dispersion of a group in a manner comparable to that of the Jews among the Gentiles after the Babylonian captivity (6th century BCE).
Jews outside of the land of Israel.

diaspora.ety: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek διασπορᾱ́ (diasporā́, “dispersion”), from διασπείρω (diaspeírō, “to scatter”), from δια- (dia-, prefix indicating motion across or in all directions) + σπείρω (speírō, “to sow”).

note.ja: ギリシャ語 diaspora（散らばること）から。dia（あちこちに）+ speirein（種をまく）。「離散」。sperm と同じ。

en: Lack of concord, agreement, harmony; disaccord.
Tension or strife resulting from a lack of agreement; dissension.

discord.ety:
Circa 1230, Middle English descorde, discorde; from Anglo-Norman, Old French descort (derivative of descorder), descorde (“disagreement”); from Latin discordia, from discors (“disagreeing, disagreement”), from dis- (“apart”) + cor, cordis (“heart”).
Verb derives from Middle English discorden, from Anglo-Norman, Old French descorder, from Latin discordāre, from discord-, as above.

ex.en: Finally, the discord between them came to an end.
ex.ja: ついに両者の間の不和は終わりになった。

ex.en: A gift of cheesecake is apparently good to soothe discord.
ex.ja: 波風を鎮めるにはチーズケーキのお土産が良いらしいですよ。

note.ja: dis（離れて）+ cord（心）。心が離れること →「不一致・不和・不協和音」。

Synonym of deity.

note.ja: divine（神の）+ -ity。ラテン語 divus（神の）。「神性・神学」。deity と同系。

en: The ability to last a long time by virtue of the power to resist stress or force.

durability.ety: From Middle English durabilite, from Old French durabilité, from Latin dūrābilitās (“durability”). Corresponding to durable + -ity.

ex.en: He checked the durability of the house before buying it.
ex.ja: 彼は家の耐久性を買う前に調べた。

ex.en: This machine is inferior to that one in durability.
ex.ja: この機械は、耐久性であの機械に劣ります。

note.ja: dur（続く）+ ability。長く続く性質 →「耐久性」。

en: British standard spelling of endeavor.
British standard spelling of endeavor.

note.ja: endeavor のイギリスのつづり。en + devoir（義務）。「努力」。

en: To enter (a name, etc.) in a register, roll or list
To enlist (someone) or make (someone) a member of.

enroll.ety: From Middle English enrollen, from Anglo-Norman enroller; by surface analysis, en- + roll.

ex.ja: 彼らは彼を陪審員として登録した。

en: The state proceeding from destiny; invincible necessity, superior to, and independent of, free and rational control.
Tendency to death, destruction or danger, as if by decree of fate.

en: A festival or similar celebration.
An experience or expression of celebratory feeling, merriment, gaiety.

festivity.ety: Inherited from Middle English festivite, from Middle French festivité, from Latin festīvitas, equivalent to festive + -ity.

ex.en: The festivities were held as usual this year.
ex.ja: お祭りは今年も例年通り開催された。

en: A utensil with spikes used to put solid food into the mouth, or to hold food down while cutting, or for serving food.
Any of several types of pronged tools for use on farms, in fields, or in the garden or lawn, such as a smaller hand fork for weeding or a…
To divide into two or more branches or copies.
To spawn a new child process by duplicating the existing process.

fork.ety: From Middle English forke (“digging fork”), from Old English force, forca (“forked instrument used to torture”), from Proto-West Germanic *furkō (“fork”), from Latin furca (“pitchfork, forked stake; gallows, beam, stake, support post, yoke”), of uncertain origin. ex.ja: 彼らはナイフとフォークで食事をする。

ex.en: There's a fork in the road here.

en: To draw in the breath suddenly, as if from a shock.
To breathe quickly or in a labored manner, as after exertion; to respire with heaving of the breast; to pant.
A short, sudden intake of breath.
The sound of a gasp.

gasp.ety: From Middle English gaspen, gayspen (“to gape, outbreathe”), related to and likely derived from Old Norse geispa (“to yawn”) or its descendant Danish gispe, which may be related to gapa (“to gape”).

ex.ja: 彼は息を切らして走り続けた。

ex.en: I ran while gasping for air.
ex.ja: 私は息を切らせて走った。

ex.en: She gasped out the news.
ex.ja: 彼女はその知らせをあえぎながら伝えた。

note.ja: 北欧語 geispa（あくびをする）から。「はっと息をのむ」。

en: A problem affecting function.
An unexpected behavior in an electrical signal, especially if the signal spontaneously returns to expected behavior after a period of time.
To experience an unexpected, typically intermittent malfunction.
To perform an exploit or recreate a bug while playing a video game.

glitch.ety:
Probably borrowed from Yiddish גליטש (glitsh), from German glitschig (“slippy”), from glitschen (“to slide, glide, slip”) + -ig (“-y”). Related to gleiten (“glide”). Cognate with French glisser (“to slip, slide, skid”).
Popularized in the 1960s, by the US space program. Attested in 1962 by American astronaut John Glenn, in reference to spikes in electrical current.

ex.en: He is raising a big stink over a minor glitch.
ex.ja: 彼はささいな故障に大騒ぎをしています。

en: A percussion instrument consisting of a metal disk that emits a loud resonant sound when struck with a soft hammer.
A metal target that emits a sound when it has been hit.
To make the sound of a gong; to ring a gong.
To halt (originally, a contestant in a talent show; later, a performer, a speaker).

ex.en: The room emptied when the gong for dinner sounded.
ex.ja: 食事のドラが鳴ると部屋はからになった。

note.ja: マレー語 gong（擬音）から。「どら」。

en: Having a slippery surface; having a surface covered with grease.
Containing a lot of grease or fat.
An annoyed or contemptuous look; a dirty look.
Wool that still contains grease and has not undergone scouring.

greasy.ety: From Middle English gresi, gressy, equivalent to grease + -y.

ex.en: What is that greasy stuff on your shirt?
ex.ja: シャツについている、べとべとしたものは何ですか。

ex.en: My hair is greasy.
ex.ja: 髪の毛がべとべとしている。

ex.en: I have greasy skin.
ex.ja: 肌が脂っぽいのです。

note.ja: grease（油脂）+ -y。「脂っこい」。

en: Feeling or showing sorrow or distress due to loss, especially the death of someone.
An act or instance of feeling or expressing grief.

ex.en: The grieving woman was consoled by her friends.
ex.ja: 悲しみに暮れるその女性は友人たちに慰められた。

ex.en: The mother was still grieving over her child's death.
ex.ja: その母親は子供の死をいまだに嘆き悲しんでいた。

en: A hot sandwich consisting of a patty of cooked ground beef or a meat substitute, in a sliced bun, usually also containing salad vegetable…
The patty used in such a sandwich.
To badly injure or damage (a fleshy part of the body).

hamburger.ety: Shortening of Hamburger sandwich, Hamburger steak, etc., the first element borrowed from German Hamburger (“native of Hamburg”), equivalent to Hamburg + -er.

ex.en: Is it OK if I eat this hamburger?
ex.ja: このハンバーガーを食べてもいいですか。

ex.en: I ate a hamburger and ordered another.
ex.ja: 私はハンバーガーを１つ食べてもう１つ注文した。

ex.en: This hamburger is better than those of that shop.
ex.ja: このハンバーガーはあの店よりおいしい。

note.ja: ドイツの都市ハンブルク（Hamburg）風のステーキから。ham（ハム）とは無関係。

en: Careful attention.
To mind; to regard with care; to take notice of; to attend to; to observe.

heed.ety: From Middle English heden, from Old English hēdan (“to heed, take care, observe, attend, guard, take charge, take possession, receive”), from Proto-West Germanic *hōdijan (“to heed, guard”), from Proto-Indo-European *kadʰ- (“to heed, protect”). Cognate with West Frisian hoedje (“to heed”), Dutch hoeden (“to heed”), German hüten (“to heed”).

ex.en: You must heed the advice of your teacher.
ex.ja: 先生のおっしゃることを注意して聞かなければなりません。

ex.en: The man gave no heed to her loud protest.
ex.ja: その男は彼女が大声で反対するのに耳を貸さなかった。

ex.en: They gave no heed to the warning.
ex.ja: 彼らは警告に全然注意を払わなかった。

note.ja: 古英語 hēdan（気をつける）から。「注意を払う」。heedless（不注意な）。

en: Extremely or shockingly ugly.
Having a very unpleasant or frightening sound.

hideous.ety:
From Middle English hidous, from Anglo-Norman hidous, from Old French hideus, hydus (“that which inspires terror”), from earlier hisdos, from Old French hisda (“horror, fear”), of uncertain and disputed origin. Probably from Proto-West Germanic *agisiþu (“horror, terror”), from Proto-West Germanic *agisōn (“to frighten, terrorise”), from Proto-Germanic *agaz (“terror, fear”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂egʰ- (“to frighten”). Cognate with Old High German egisa, egidī (“horror”), Old English egesa (“fear, dread”), Gothic 𐌰𐌲𐌹𐍃 (agis, “fear, terror”).
Alternative etymology cites possible derivatio

ex.en: A hideous monster used to live there.
ex.ja: 以前恐ろしい怪物が住んでいた。

ex.en: Tom had a hideous hangover.
ex.ja: トムがとんでもない二日酔いをしてしまいました。

en: A circular band of metal used to bind a barrel.
Any circular band or ring.
To bind or fasten using a hoop.
To clasp; to encircle; to surround.

hoop.ety: From Middle English hoop, hoope, from Old English hōp (“mound, raised land; in combination, circular object”), from Proto-Germanic *hōpą (“bend, bow, arch”) (compare Saterland Frisian Houp (“hoop”), Dutch hoep (“hoop”), Old Norse hóp (“bay, inlet”)), from Proto-Indo-European *kāb- (“to bend”) (compare Lithuanian kabė (“hook”), Old Church Slavonic кѫпъ (kǫpŭ, “hill, island”)). More at camp.

ex.en: I'd jump through hoops for you.
ex.ja: 君のためならたとえ火の中水の中。

note.ja: 古英語 hōp（輪）から。「輪・（バスケットの）リング」。

zh: 充滿創意的 /充满创意的
想像力豐富的 /想像力丰富的

en: Having a lively or creative imagination.
Tending to be fanciful or inventive.

imaginative.ety: From Middle English ymagynatif, from Middle French imaginatif, from Medieval Latin imāginātīvus. By surface analysis, imagine + -ative.

ex.en: He used to be an imaginative boy.
ex.ja: 彼は想像力のたくましい少年であった。

ex.en: He is a very imaginative writer.
ex.ja: 彼は非常に想像力にとんだ作家です。

ex.en: This novel is very imaginative.
ex.ja: この小説は想像力に富んでいる。

en: Not perfect.
Unisexual: having either male (with stamens) or female (with pistil) flowers, but not with both.
Something having a minor flaw.
A tense of verbs used in describing a past action that is incomplete or continuous.
to make imperfect

ex.en: Everyone is imperfect, and that's OK.
ex.ja: 誰にでも欠点はある。それでいいのよ。

ex.en: Partly because he could not receive enough information, Harper's description remains imperfect.
ex.ja: 十分な情報を受け取ることができなかったという理由も一部にはあって、ハーパーの描写は不完全なものにとどまっている。

note.ja: im（否定）+ perfect（完全な）。「不完全な」。perfect は per + facere（すっかり作る）。

en: Suggested indirectly, without being directly expressed; Implied.
Contained in the essential nature of something but not openly shown.

implicit.ety: From Middle French implicite, from Latin implicitus, past participle of implico (“to infold, involve, entangle”); see implicate.

ex.en: We had an implicit agreement that we would support each other.
ex.ja: 我々には互いに支持しあおうという暗黙の了解があった。

ex.en: There's nothing equivalent to "already" in the English version, but maybe it's implicit?
ex.ja: 「もう」の表現が英文にないけど、それって、暗黙的なモノ？

note.ja: im（中に）+ plic（折る）+ it。中に折り込まれた →「暗黙の・それとなく示された」。explicit（明白な）と対。

en: A body of water let into a coast, such as a bay, cove, fjord or estuary.
A passage that leads into a cavity.
To let in; admit.
To insert; inlay.

inlet.ety: From Middle English inlāte (“inlet, entrance”), from inleten (“to let in”), equivalent to in- + let. Compare Low German inlat (“inlet”), German Einlass (“inlet, entrance”).

note.ja: in（中に）+ let（入れる）。「海が入り込んだ所」→「入り江・注入口」。

en: Expressing or feeling little or no concern, care, compassion, or consideration for the feelings, emotions, sentiments, or concerns of oth…
Not expressing normal physical feeling.

ex.ja: あの人、鈍感よね？

ex.ja: トムって無神経だと思う。

ex.en: I think Tom is insensitive.
ex.ja: トムって無神経だと思う。

note.ja: in（否定）+ sensitive（敏感な）。「無神経な・鈍感な」。

en: A person who lives on an island.

islander.ety: From island + -er. Displaced Middle English insulane (“islander”), from Latin īnsulānus (“islander”).

ex.en: The islanders are asking us for help.
ex.ja: その島の人々は我々の助けを求めている。

ex.en: The islanders are kind.
ex.ja: 島の人たちは、優しいです。

ex.en: The islanders are friendly.
ex.ja: 島の人たちは、優しいです。

note.ja: island（島）+ -er。「島民」。island の s は isle の影響で綴りに入った。

en: The top stone of an arch.
Something on which other things depend for support.
To distort (an image) by projecting it onto a surface at an angle, which for example causes a square to look like a trapezoid.
To double the cost price in order to determine the retail price; to apply a markup of 100%.

keystone.ety:
From key + stone.
Definition 4 (retail) possibly originated in the jewelry industry in the magazine called "Jewelers' Circular-Keystone".

note.ja: key（鍵・要）+ stone（石）。アーチの頂上に入れて全体を支える石 →「要石・要」。

en: Praise; accolades.
Credit for one's achievements.
An interjection indicating praise or approval or as an acknowledgement of a laudable achievement.
To give praise or accolades.

kudos.ety: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek κῦδος (kûdos, “praise, renown”).

ex.en: Kudos for your outstanding achievement!
ex.ja: 素晴らしい業績に拍手を送ります。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 kydos（栄光）から。「称賛」。単数扱い。

ja: （in lieu of で）〜の代わりに

en: A place or stead.

lieu.ety:
Etymology tree

Borrowed from Middle French lieu, from Old French leu, from Latin locum, accusative of locus (“place”). Doublet of locus. Attested earlier and in Middle English only as part of the partially calqued phrase in lieu of.

en: The state or property of being liquid.
The degree of which something is in high supply and demand, making it easily convertible to cash.

liquidity.ety: From liquid + -ity, from Latin liquiditas. In their financial and economic senses, this and various associated terms all involve portraying assets figuratively as if they were liquids and solids, dissolving the solids with solvents, freezing and thawing, and so on.

note.ja: liquid（液体の・現金化しやすい）+ -ity。「流動性」。

en: A low- to medium-viscosity topical preparation intended for application to unbroken skin.
To cover or treat with a lotion.

lotion.ety:
Etymology tree
Latin lōtiōnembor.
Middle English locion
English lotion
Inherited from Middle English locion, borrowed from Latin lōtiōnem. See lave. Doublet of lavation.

ex.en: She is putting on some face lotion.
ex.ja: 彼女は化粧水をつけている。

ex.en: I need hand lotion.
ex.ja: ハンドローションが欲しいのよ。

en: Of or pertaining to the theology of Martin Luther (1483–1546) or his followers, or the Lutheran church.
A member of any of the Christian churches which identify with the theology of Martin Luther.

Lutheran.ety:
From the surname of German theologian and ecclesiastical reformer Martin Luther (1483–1546) + -an. Probably immediately from Renaissance Latin Lutheranus, or German Lutheraner.
Luther is from an Old High German given name, from liut (“people”) + heri (“army”) (from Proto-Germanic *harjaz (“army; commander, warrior”), from Proto-Indo-European *kóryos (“war; troops”), from *ker- (“army”)).

note.ja: 宗教改革者マルティン・ルター（Martin Luther）の名前から。

en: The criminal offence of maiming (“seriously wounding”) a person such that their ability to defend or protect themselves is weakened or co…
The criminal offence of maiming a person by depriving them of the use of any of their limbs.

mayhem.ety:
The noun is derived from Late Middle English mayehem, maihem, a late form of maym, maim (“disfigurement, injury, mutilation; disfigured person”) (whence modern English maim (noun)), from Anglo-Norman mahaim, mahainne (“mutilation”), and Old French mehaing, meshaing (“bodily harm, loss of limb”).
The verb is partly:
* from Late Middle English mahaym, maheyme, a late form of maimen, maymen (“to injure seriously, mutilate, maim; to damage; to destroy; to afflict with disease; to dispossess”) (whence modern English maim (verb)), from Anglo-Norman mahaigner, mahimer, Middle French mehaignier, and O

note.ja: 古フランス語 mahaignier（傷つける）から。maim（不具にする）と同じ。「傷害罪」→「大混乱」。

en: Wrongly; erroneously.
By accident; by mistake; in error (without intention to do so).

mistakenly.ety:
Etymology tree
English mistaken
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English mistakenly
From mistaken + -ly.

ex.en: Sorry! I mistakenly clicked on "Send" before I was finished.
ex.ja: すみません、途中でうっかり送信ボタンを押してしまいました。

ex.en: Sorry! I mistakenly clicked on "Send".
ex.ja: ごめん！間違って「送信」クリックしちゃった。

ex.en: I've mistakenly deleted the party information and registration you sent to me.
ex.ja: パーティーの案内と申込書を間違って削除してしまいました。

note.ja: mistaken（誤った）+ -ly。「誤って」。

en: Commonwealth standard spelling of mold.
Commonwealth standard spelling of mold.

mould.ety: Via Middle English molde, moulde (“mould, cast”) and Old French modle, from Latin modulus.

A person who displays nostalgia for something.

ex.ja: 夕暮れの商店街を歩くと、どこか懐かしい気持ちになる。

ex.en: She indulged herself in nostalgic memories.
ex.ja: 彼女は懐かしい思い出にふけった。

note.ja: nostalgia（郷愁）+ -ic。ギリシャ語 nostos（帰郷）+ algos（痛み）。「懐かしい」。

en: Burdensome or difficult to bear.
Tyrannical or exercising unjust power.

ex.ja: 彼は、前の政府に劣らず圧制的な現政府に公然と反抗している。

en: The act of providing approval and support; backing; championship.
Customers collectively; clientele; business.
To support by being a patron of.
To be a regular customer or client of; to patronize

patronage.ety: From Middle English patronage, from Old French patronage (modern French patronage). Equivalent to patron + -age. Piecewise doublet of patternage.

ex.en: We really thank you for your patronage.
ex.ja: 日頃のご愛顧にお礼申し上げます。

ex.en: Thank you for your patronage.
ex.ja: 毎度ごひいきにありがとうございます。

ex.en: Isamu Kobayashi received the patronage of Rohan Koda.
ex.ja: 小林勇は幸田 露伴の愛顧を受けた。

note.ja: patron（後援者）+ -age。ラテン語 patronus（保護者）、pater（父）。「後援・ひいき」。

en: The highest point.
A tall, sharp and craggy rock or mountain.
To place on a pinnacle.
To build or furnish with a pinnacle or pinnacles.

pinnacle.ety: From Middle English, borrowed from Old French pinacle, pinnacle, from Late Latin pinnāculum (“a peak, pinnacle”), from Latin pinna (“a pinnacle”); see pin. Doublet of panache.

note.ja: ラテン語 pinnaculum（小さな羽・尖塔）から。pinna（羽）。「尖塔」→「頂点」。

en: To be successful; to succeed; to be fortunate or prosperous; to thrive; to make gain.
To grow; to increase.

prosper.ety: From Old French prosperer, from Latin prosperō (“to render happy”), from prosperus (“prosperous”), from Proto-Italic *prosparos, from Proto-Indo-European *speh₁- (“to succeed”), whence also Latin spēs (“hope, expectation”).

ex.en: The good will not necessarily prosper.
ex.ja: 善人が必ずしも成功するとは限らない。

ex.en: Not all good men will prosper.
ex.ja: 善人必ずしも栄える者でない。

ex.en: My business is prospering.
ex.ja: 私の商売は繁盛している。

note.ja: ラテン語 prosperare（成功させる）から。pro + spes（希望）。「希望どおりになる」→「栄える」。prosperity。

en: A trembling or shaking.
An earthquake, a trembling of the ground with force.
To tremble or shake.
To be in a state of fear, shock, amazement, etc., such as might cause one to tremble.

quake.ety: From Middle English quaken, from Old English cwacian (“to quake, tremble, chatter”), from Proto-Germanic *kwakōną (“to shake, quiver, tremble”), itself likely of imitative origin. en: Of descriptions or distinctions based on some quality rather than on some quantity.
Of a form of analysis that yields the identity of a compound.
Something qualitative.

qualitative.ety: From Late Latin (or Medieval Latin) quālitātīvus. Equivalent to quality + -ative.

note.ja: ラテン語 qualitas（性質）から。qualis（どのような）。「質的な」。quantitative（量的な）と対。

note.ja: フランス語 reconnaissance（見分けること）から。re + connaître（知る）。「偵察」。recognize と同じ。

en: One who rules in place of the monarch, especially because the monarch is too young, absent, or disabled.
A member of a municipal or civic body of governors, especially in certain European cities.
Ruling; governing; regnant.
Exercising vicarious authority.

regent.ety: From Middle English regent, from Anglo-Norman regent, Middle French regent, and their source, Latin regēns (“ruling; ruler, governor, prince”), present participle of regō (“to govern, to steer”).

From reluctant + -ly.

ex.ja: 彼はいやいや彼女に会いに行った。

ex.ja: 彼は僕の提案にしぶしぶ同意した。

ex.en: He reluctantly went to see her.
ex.ja: 彼はいやいや彼女に会いに行った。

en: An interpretation or performance of an artwork, especially a musical score or musical work.
A given visual reproduction of something.
To surrender or hand over (a person or thing); especially, for one jurisdiction to do so to another.

rendition.ety: From obsolete French rendition, alteration (after rendre (“to render”)) of reddition (“reddition”). Many senses influenced by render.

note.ja: render（表現する・引き渡す）+ -ition。ラテン語 reddere（返す）。「演奏・表現・引き渡し」。

sham.ety:
Probably a dialectal form of shame.
Alternatively, sham is a term that is used to describe the bottom thick base of a glass, usually a wine or stem glass, where the stem meets the bulbous shape bowl. Glass manufacturers would increase the "sham" to deceive customers into thinking a glass holds more than it actually does. For example, a manufacturer would mold a 12oz glass with a larger "sham" in the base to reduce the volume of the glasses to fit 10-11oz of liquid. By increasing the bulge in the base, usually where the stem meets the glass, it is almost impossible to visually distinguish the d

To generate, bring into being, especially nonmammalian beings in very large numbers.

Mushroom mycelium prepared for (aided) propagation.

spawn.ety: Recorded since 1413; from Middle English spawnen, from Anglo-Norman espaundre, from Old French espandre, from Latin expandere (“stretch out; spread out”, verb). Doublet of expand. Compare also Middle English spalden, spolden, spawden (“to cut open (a fish)”).

A small, round object with a hole to allow it to be threaded on a cord or wire, particularly for decorative purposes.
To form into a bead.
To apply beads to.

bead.ety:
From Middle English bede (“a prayer”), also “a bead for counting prayers” in a peire of bedes (literally “a pair of beads”), from Old English bedu, bed, ġebed (“a request, entreaty, prayer”), from Proto-West Germanic *bedu, *bed, *gabed, from Proto-Germanic *bedō, *bedą.

berth.ety:
The noun is derived from Late Middle English birth (“(nautical) bearing away or off, clearance, berth”). Further etymology uncertain, but probably from beren (“to carry (away), bear”) + -th (suffix denoting a condition, quality, state of being, etc., forming nouns); if so, the English word is analysable as bear + -th (suffix forming nouns from verbs), and is a piecewise doublet of birth.
The verb is derived from the noun.

blackmail.ety:
From black + mail (“a piece of money”). Compare Middle English blak rente (“a type of blackmail levied by Irish chieftains”).
The word is variously derived from the tribute paid by English and Scottish border dwellers to border reivers in return for immunity from raids and other harassment. This tribute was paid in goods or labour, in Latin reditus nigri (“black mail”); the opposite is blanche firmes or reditus albi (“white rent”), denoting payment by silver.
McKay derives it from two Scottish Gaelic words blàthaich, pronounced (the th silent) bl-aich, "to protect" and màl (“tribute, payment”)

ex.ja: トムはメアリーに脅迫されていた。

note.ja: black（黒い・不正な）+ mail（年貢・地代）。スコットランドの山賊が取り立てた保護料から「恐喝」。

cafeteria.ety: Borrowed from Mexican Spanish cafetería (“coffeehouse”), from cafetera (“coffee maker”), from French cafetière, from café, from Ottoman Turkish قهوه (kahve) (Turkish kahve), from Arabic قَهْوَة (qahwa, “coffee”). Doublet of cafetière.

canary.ety: From French canarie, from Spanish canario, from the Latin Canariae insulae (“Canary Islands”) (Spanish Islas Canarias); from the largest island Insula Canaria (“Dog Island" or "Canine Island”), named for its dogs, from canārius (“canine”), from canis (“dog”).

ex.ja: １つがいのカナリアだけが彼女の友達であった。
